summary: Hold: MIT, no install scripts and one runtime dependency keep @antv/x6-plugin-stencil 2.1.5 a low-surface plugin for the legacy X6 stencil role, but absent provenance, a conflicting release date and an unrecorded browser baseline block adoption today.
reasoning: The requirement is the legacy graph application, which already uses this plugin alongside @antv/x6 and the other X6 plugins; this review asks whether to keep, upgrade or replace it, and whether D3 is a better fit.

The plugin is bound to the X6 v2 suite: peer_dependencies is @antv/x6 ^2.x and its single runtime dependency is @antv/x6-plugin-dnd ^2.x, so it is not a standalone renderer and cannot be swapped for D3 without also replacing the core graph engine.
License is MIT in both npm facts and the GitHub repository metadata, satisfying the requirement's permissive-license constraint at the package level; the full transitive tree was not audited.

No advisories are recorded in dossier.vulnerabilities, and has_install_script is false with an empty install_scripts array, so the advisory and install-script constraints are met for this package as measured.

npm_provenance is false and the dossier's provenance_note says no npm attestation was found; the requirement permits this only if exact versions are pinned and the gap recorded, which is not yet part of an adoption decision.

Release recency is unresolved: the package's latest_version 2.1.5 is dated 2024-01-10, while facts.last_publish is 2026-09-21 and versions_count is 8. The dossier does not say which release the later timestamp refers to, so the 12-month maintenance constraint cannot be confirmed from this data.
The repository is not archived, was pushed on 2026-10-23, has 6751 stars and 156 open issues, which shows activity but not a confirmed release of this plugin within the last 12 months.
Weekly downloads are 2931 and the npm metadata lists 64 maintainers; a broad maintainer set reduces bus-factor risk but widens publish access and complicates release consistency.
Footprint is small: 235 KB unpacked, one runtime dependency, bundled types and dual ESM/CJS formats; install_size_kb was not measured, so the installed size is unknown.
No browser or runtime baseline for the legacy application is recorded in the requirement or dossier, and engines is null, so compatibility with the existing baseline is unverified rather than passed.

No CI publish workflow evidence was collected; absent provenance does not prove there is no CI publishing, so the hard-failure cap for that condition is not applied, but the release-integrity gap remains.
Rubric scoring: security 24/30, release integrity 12/25, maintenance 12/20, fit 12/15, footprint 7/10, totalling 67, which falls in the 60-79 hold band.

No hard failure is confirmed: no unfixed high or critical advisory is recorded, no install script is present, and unmaintained status is not established because the release dates conflict; the verdict is driven by incomplete evidence, not by a confirmed blocker.
caveats: Without npm provenance, the requirement demands pinning 2.1.5 exactly and recording the gap; an unpinned ^2.x range would not satisfy it.
The peer range is @antv/x6 ^2.x only; if the legacy suite moves to X6 v3, this plugin is outside its declared peer range and a v3-compatible release is not evidenced in the dossier.
The 2024-01-10 version date and the 2026-09-21 last_publish timestamp disagree, so confirm the intended artifact before pinning.
No compatibility test was run against the legacy browser/runtime baseline, which is not recorded anywhere in the dossier.
Only this package's advisories were collected; advisories in the @antv/x6-plugin-dnd or @antv/x6 tree were not audited for this request.
Install size was not measured, so disk and bundle impact cannot be stated beyond the 235 KB unpacked figure.
The request asks about D3 as an alternative; the dossier contains no comparison data for D3, so that question is unanswered here.
Sixty-four npm maintainers share publish rights, so release provenance and review discipline depend on repository policy that was not measured.

evidence.label: CI publishing
evidence.detail: No publish workflow or CI release evidence was collected for this package, and the dossier warnings array is empty. CI publishing is therefore unmeasured, so the no-CI-publishing hard-failure cap is not applied either way.

evidence.label: npm provenance
evidence.detail: npm_provenance is false and provenance_note states that no npm attestation was found. No attested version is evidenced, so the requirement's provenance-or-pin constraint is only satisfiable by pinning 2.1.5 exactly and recording the gap.

evidence.label: Known advisories
evidence.detail: dossier.vulnerabilities is empty; no unfixed high or critical advisory is recorded for 2.1.5. Only this package's advisory data was collected, not the full dependency tree.

evidence.label: Maintenance and release recency
evidence.detail: Latest version 2.1.5 is dated 2024-01-10, but facts.last_publish is 2026-09-21 with versions_count 8, so the dossier conflicts on recency and the 12-month release constraint is unconfirmed. The repository is not archived, was pushed 2026-10-23, and has 156 open issues and 6751 stars; weekly downloads are 2931.

evidence.label: Dependency footprint
evidence.detail: One runtime dependency (@antv/x6-plugin-dnd ^2.x) plus a peer dependency on @antv/x6 ^2.x; 235 KB unpacked. install_size_kb is null, so the installed size was not measured.

evidence.label: TypeScript types and formats
evidence.detail: Types are bundled and the package ships dual ESM/CJS formats, so no separate @types package is required.

evidence.label: Fit to the legacy graph requirement
evidence.detail: The plugin is suite-bound: peer dependency @antv/x6 ^2.x and runtime dependency @antv/x6-plugin-dnd ^2.x. It preserves the existing legacy stencil role rather than replacing the X6 engine, and it is not interchangeable with D3. The legacy browser/runtime baseline is unrecorded and engines is null, so compatibility and behaviour preservation were not tested.

evidence.label: License
evidence.detail: MIT is reported in npm facts and in the GitHub repository metadata, which meets the requirement's permissive-license constraint for this package. The transitive tree's licenses were not audited.
